rules.rule: a flow whose source, target or data owner is not a system of the systems file, when one is given
a flow end or a system whose location is empty or none of cloud, on-premise and saas and their names and the 1 alias of the configuration
a flow end whose location differs from the location of the same system in the systems file or in an earlier flow
a flow whose pattern is empty or none of api, event, file, batch, database and ipaas and their names and the 1 alias of the configuration
a flow whose direction, trigger, authentication, encryption, error handling, monitoring or personal data flag holds a value that is none of the names of src/vocabulary.js
a flow whose source, target and data an earlier flow already has
a flow whose id an earlier flow already has
a two-way flow with no data owner, or two flows that carry the same data in opposite directions without one data owner named by both
a hybrid flow, or a flow with a SaaS end, whose transport encryption is no or not stated
a hybrid flow, or a flow with a SaaS end, whose authentication is none, basic or not stated
a hybrid flow, or a flow with a SaaS end, whose authentication is an API key or a shared access signature
a flow with the personal data flag set and no transport encryption
a flow that names a retry policy and no idempotency key or method
a real-time flow with an empty retry policy or none
a scheduled flow with no interval, or with an interval the tool does not read
a flow with an empty error handling or none
a flow whose monitoring is no or empty
a flow with an empty owner, or a flows file with no owner column
a system connected directly to more than 4 other systems
a flow or system with the wrong number of fields, no source, target or name, a system named twice, or a value of the wrong kind
a flows or systems file that the tool could not read as UTF-8 text
a flows or systems file that the CSV or JSON reader refuses, or whose header or shape is not that of its role

findings.found: the system "fleet-tracker" has the location "private cloud", which is not cloud, on-premise or saas
findings.fix: write cloud, on-premise or saas, add the system to the systems file with its location, or add the name your team uses to locationAliases in the configuration

basis.text: cloud computing gives network access on demand to a shared pool of configurable resources, and the definition sets it out in essential characteristics, three service models and four deployment models
basis.source: NIST SP 800-145, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing (NIST CSRC)

basis.text: the four deployment models are private, community, public and hybrid
basis.source: NIST SP 800-145, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing (NIST CSRC)

basis.text: a private cloud serves one organization and may sit on or off its premises, while a public cloud sits on the premises of the provider
basis.source: NIST SP 800-145, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, full text (NIST)

basis.text: in software as a service the consumer uses applications the provider runs on its own infrastructure, and controls neither the infrastructure nor, beyond some settings, the application
basis.source: NIST SP 800-145, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, full text (NIST)

findings.own: a location is cloud, on-premise or saas, by one of the names of src/vocabulary.js or locationAliases; private cloud is not read as either, because a private cloud may be on or off the premises; an empty location is taken from the systems file when it lists the system, and otherwise reported

findings.found: the flow "F03" is two-way between ledger-erp and crm-suite and names no data owner, so both can write customers
findings.fix: name the system of record of the data in the data owner column of every flow that carries it, and let only that system write the data

basis.text: a point-to-point channel makes sure that only one receiver consumes a given message, even when several receivers listen
a receiver can get the same message more than once even when it was sent once, so it either removes duplicates or is built so a repeated message does no harm

findings.own: a two-way flow with no data owner, and a flow from A to B with the same data as an earlier flow from B to A when the two do not name the same data owner, are reported: each side can overwrite the other and an update can go round in a loop

findings.found: the flow "F03" crosses from on-premise to saas, a hybrid flow, and authenticates with basic, a user name and a password
findings.fix: authenticate the flow with OAuth 2.0, mutual TLS or a managed identity, and write it in the authentication column

basis.text: a hybrid cloud is two or more distinct cloud infrastructures that stay separate entities but are bound together by technology that lets data and applications move between them
basis.source: NIST SP 800-145, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, full text (NIST)

basis.text: cloud capabilities are reached over the network through standard mechanisms, from many kinds of client
basis.source: NIST SP 800-145, The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing, full text (NIST)

findings.own: a flow crosses a boundary when one end is on-premise and the other in the cloud or a SaaS application (a hybrid flow), when one end is in the cloud and the other a SaaS application, or when both ends are SaaS applications; a flow between two on-premise systems or two cloud systems does not; such a flow with authentication none, basic (a user name and a password) or no authentication stated is reported

findings.found: the flow "F03" retries (3 tries) and names no idempotency key or method, so a repeated delivery can write a record twice
findings.fix: name the idempotency key or method the target uses to drop a repeated record, such as a message id it stores or an upsert on a business key

basis.text: a receiver can get the same message more than once even when it was sent once, so it either removes duplicates or is built so a repeated message does no harm
a message is kept in a store at each step and not removed until the next store holds it, so a failure on the way does not lose it

findings.own: a flow with a retry policy (any text but none or no) and no idempotency key or method; a retry after a lost reply sends the same record again, and without idempotency the target can write it twice

findings.found: the flow "F05" is scheduled and names no interval
findings.fix: write the interval, such as every 15 min, hourly or a cron expression

basis.text: a message is kept in a store at each step and not removed until the next store holds it, so a failure on the way does not lose it

findings.own: a scheduled flow needs an interval in the interval column or with its trigger: a number with a unit of time, a word such as hourly or nightly, or a cron expression; without one nobody can tell how stale the data of the target may be
